# R1 results — schema and evidence inventory

## Raw artifacts (git-ignored, regenerated by protocol)

Produced under `build/parquet-results/` by `run-bench.sh`:

* `warmup-pass.json`, `measure-pass.json` — Google Benchmark JSON (library
  1.9.1). Layout: `context` (host toolchain identity), then `benchmarks[]`.
  Per-run entries carry `name`, `aggregate_name: null`, `real_time`,
  `cpu_time`, `iterations`, and flat per-iteration counters (`rows`,
  `cells`, `columns_read`, `io_calls`, `requested_bytes`, `returned_bytes`,
  `read_errors`, `open_meta_ms`, `read_ms`). Aggregate entries are named
  `<bench>_mean|_median|_stddev|_cv` with `aggregate_name` set; time unit is
  ns wall (`real_time`) and ns CPU (`cpu_time`).
* `trace-*.jsonl` — request traces: header line (`type`, `version`,
  `dataset_sha`, `dataset_path`, `workload`, `arm`, `file_size`), then one
  line per request (`i`, `offset`, `requested`, `returned`, `ok`).
* `summary.txt` — human summary (same text as `results/r1/summary.txt`).
* `read-path-evidence.txt` — nm/strace provenance for the byte movers.

## Committed evidence (this directory, `results/r1/`)

Repository policy (AGENTS rule 6) keeps benchmark JSON and perf traces out
of Git, so what is committed here is the human-readable evidence plus the
identity records needed to regenerate and re-verify the rest:

* `summary.txt` — sampled-pass table + attribution ratios (identical copy
  of `build/parquet-results/summary.txt`).
* `run-manifest.txt` — provenance for the sampled pass: `DUDUDU_SHA`,
  `SLUICE_SHA`, profile, SDK prefix, toolchain, repetitions, kernel, and
  the SHA-256 + byte size of both datasets.
* `read-path-evidence.txt` — object-level (which TU issues `pread` vs which
  references `sluice::blocking::read_at`), dynamic strace counts, and the
  fault-injection pointer to the oracle test.
* `manifest-small-none.json`, `manifest-medium-none.json` — dataset freeze
  records (path, bytes, sha256, seed, generator, Arrow version).

The raw artifacts stay under ignored `build/parquet-results/`; the trace
files' identity for this round (regenerable by rerunning the protocol at
`run-manifest.txt`'s commit) is: `trace-medium-t3.jsonl` and
`trace-medium-t3-p2.jsonl` over the medium dataset, each with 57 requests
and 181996415 requested/returned bytes, byte-identical request lists
between the arms — that identity, not the files, is the cross-arm check.

## Frozen numbers this round (sampled pass, mean wall, host disclosed in
protocol.md; provenance in `run-manifest.txt`)

| workload | dataset | P0 | P1 | P2 | wrapper tax | sluice effect | e2e |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1_meta | small | 51491 ns | 51102 ns | 51955 ns | −0.76% | +1.67% | +0.90% |
| T1_meta | medium | 65101 ns | 65284 ns | 65273 ns | +0.28% | −0.02% | +0.26% |
| T2_projection | small | 1501187 ns | 1494051 ns | 1500397 ns | −0.48% | +0.42% | −0.05% |
| T2_projection | medium | 35815394 ns | 35883469 ns | 35860500 ns | +0.19% | −0.06% | +0.13% |
| T3_fullscan | small | 5185013 ns | 5197245 ns | 5130995 ns | +0.24% | −1.27% | −1.04% |
| T3_fullscan | medium | 121175218 ns | 121319434 ns | 121799091 ns | +0.12% | +0.40% | +0.51% |
| Replay I/O-only | medium | 191555734 ns (native) | — | 189960508 ns (sluice) | — | −0.83% | — |

Per-benchmark CV on the sampled pass: 1.1–7.6% (T3/small is the noisy end;
the load-bearing T3/medium rows sit at 3.0–4.0%). The 4-thread full-scan
variant ran at 10–16% CV and is exploratory only. Every attribution ratio
above is within noise under the decision rule below.

Decision rule for "within noise" in the table above: a ratio is called
within noise when its magnitude is below the larger of the two arms' CVs
(one relative standard deviation of the mean over 10 samples). No
p-quantiles or significance tests are reported because the sample count
does not support them.

Reading, honestly: on a warm cache and one synchronous thread, the three
arms are statistically indistinguishable everywhere that matters, and the
I/O-only replay agrees. Wrapper tax ≈ 0 (P1 is the same `pread` primitive
as `ReadableFile`'s). Sluice effect ≈ 0 — `read_at` costs no more than
`pread` for this request stream (large sequential-ish positional reads, 57
requests for 174 MB). Nothing here licenses a claim that Sluice is faster
or slower in production conditions; it licenses "no measurable synchronous
overhead on this workload, on this host, warm cache", plus the request
profiles themselves. The interesting bottlenecks to test next are (1) cold
cache / small random reads, where per-call fixed costs matter, (2) the
async request path (Sluice ThreadPool/io_uring), which is exactly what the
D-arms round is for, and (3) buffered-stream reader settings that change
the request-size distribution.
